column5: Imagine: one reindeer walks into camp, and it starts making copies.
You are standing in a camp in a green clearing, with the campers.
One at the edge of the clearing.
You count them yourself, to be sure you are awake.
You give up counting, and start watching instead.
The largest real herds reach five hundred thousand animals.
They stand shoulder to shoulder, and every hour, thirty-two more arrive.
Even so, it is only a fraction of a real herd.
But a herd that stays in one place eats the ground bare.
A migrating herd walks up to five thousand kilometres a year, eating as it goes.
After eight hours, the arrivals stop, and the herd stands still.
Two hundred and fifty-seven reindeer surround the camp.
By the end of the day, the herd has not moved.
There was simply no space left.
